From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: çafë, cafe, CAFE, cafè, and Café

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
café
Wikipedia

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cafe
  • caffè (Italianate)
  • caffe (Italianate)
  • caffé (Italianate, nonstandard)
  • caff (UK, informal)

Etymology

[edit]

Unadapted borrowing from French café (“coffee; coffee shop”). Doublet of caffè and coffee.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (US) IPA(key): /ˌkæˈfeɪ/
  • (UK) IPA(key): /ˈkæfeɪ/
  • Audio (US):(file)
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Homophone: CAFE
  • Rhymes: -æfeɪ, -eɪ

Noun

[edit]

café (plural cafés)

  2. A coffee shop; an establishment selling coffee and sometimes other non-alcoholic beverages, simple meals or snacks, with a facility to consume them on the premises.
  3. (Canada) A small restaurant of any genre.
    • 1982, Joni Mitchell, “Chinese Café / Unchained Melody”:

Synonyms

[edit]
  • (coffee shop): caff (British slang), coffeehouse, coffee shop, tea shop, coffee bar

[edit]
  • bar
  • bistro
  • cafeteria
  • restaurant

    Noun

    café m (plural cafés)

    1. coffee
      O día estaba frío, e despois de xantar os convidados dixeron que non lles sentaría nada mal un café.

    3. coffee plant

    Polish

    Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
    café
    Wikipedia pl

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Unadapted borrowing from French café. Doublet of kawa.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /kaˈfɛ/
    • Rhymes: -ɛ
    • Syllabification: ca‧fé

    Noun

    [edit]

    café n (indeclinable)

    1. café, coffee shop (establishment selling coffee and sometimes other non-alcoholic beverages, simple meals or snacks, with a facility to consume them on the premises)
      Synonym: kawiarnia

    Etymology

    [edit]
    Etymology tree
    Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa)bor.
    Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve)bor.
    Italian caffèbor.
    French cafébor.
    Portuguese café

      Borrowed from French café, from Italian caffè, from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve) (Turkish kahve), from Classical Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa, “coffee”).[1][2]

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kaˈfɛ/
      • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kɐˈfɛ/

      • (Alentejo, some speakers) IPA(key): /kɐˈfɛj/
      • Audio (Brazil):(file)
      • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
      • Rhymes: -ɛ
      • Hyphenation: ca‧fé

      Noun

      [edit]

      café m (countable and uncountable, plural cafés)

      1. (uncountable) coffee (beverage)
        O café é uma das bebidas mais consumidas no mundo.
        Coffee is one of the most consumed beverages in the world.
      2. coffee (a serving of this beverage)
      3. coffee bean
      4. coffee (powder made by roasting and grinding the seeds)
      5. coffee (any plant of the genus Coffea)
        Synonyms: cafezeiro, cafeeiro
      6. café; coffee shop (establishment selling coffee and sometimes other non-alcoholic beverages)
        Gosto muito deste café.
        I like this café very much.
      7. coffee (pale brown color)
      8. (Brazil) ellipsis of café da manhã (“breakfast”)
        Saí tão depressa de casa que até esqueci de tomar café.
        I left home so hurriedly that I even forgot to have breakfast.
      9. (Brazil) ellipsis of café da tarde

      Etymology

      [edit]
      Etymology tree
      Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa)bor.
      Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve)bor.
      Italian caffèbor.
      French cafébor.
      Spanish café

        Borrowed from French café, or less likely directly from Italian caffè.

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
        • IPA(key): /kaˈfe/ [kaˈfe]
        • Audio (Bolivia):(file)
        • Audio (Colombia):(file)
        • Rhymes: -e
        • Syllabification: ca‧fé

        Adjective

        [edit]

        café m or f (masculine and feminine plural café or cafés)

        1. brown

        Noun

        [edit]

        café m (plural cafés)

        1. coffee
          • 1705, Francisco Sobrino, Dicionario nuevo de las lenguas española y francesa, volume 1, Bruxelles: F. Foppens, page 69b:
            Café, m. Caffé
            Café = coffee
          • 1726, Benito Jerónimo Feijóo, Theatro critico universal, volume 1, Madrid: L. F. Mojados, page 129f.:
            Monſ. Ducan, Dotor de Mompeller, refiere de otro famoſo Medico Francès, que recetaba el Caphè vniverſalmente à todos ſus enfermos.
            [Monsieur Ducan, doctor de Mompeller, refiere de otro famoso médico francés, que recetaba el café universalmente a todos sus enfermos.]
            Mr. Ducan, doctor of Montpellier, refers to another famous French doctor, who prescribed coffee to all of his patiens altogether.
          • 1740, Bernardo de Ulloa, Restablecimiento de las fabricas i comercio español, volume 1, Madrid: A. Marin, page 161f.:
            Explica las mercaderias que los Olandeſes ſacan de varias partes […] Azucar, Cafè, y Thè, Ambar, […]
            [Explica las mercaderías que los holandeses sacan de varias partes […] azúcar, café y té, ámbar, […] ]
            Explains the goods that the Dutch take from various places, […] sugar, coffee and tea, amber, […]
          • 18th c., Jorge Juan, Antonio de Ulloa, Noticias secretas de América, London: R. Taylor, published 1826, page 602:
            La Francia estableció en sus colonias de Santo Domingo y la Martinica el comercio de café para excusarse de traerlo del Oriente
            France established coffee trade on its colonies of Saint-Domingue and Martinique to avoid having to take it from the East
        2. cafe, coffee shop
        3. brown
